When the new borehole was sunk at Ugwuoba, the women of the village no longer had to walk four kilometres to the stream before dawn. For years, girls like Adaeze had arrived at school tired and late, their uniforms splashed with mud. Now the water came from a tap beside the market square, and the line of yellow jerrycans that once wound down the hill disappeared almost overnight.

Not everyone was pleased at first. Some elders said the stream had served their fathers well and that water from under the ground could not be trusted. The health worker, Mrs Obi, invited them to the clinic, where she showed them how many children had suffered from stomach illness the previous year. Most of those cases, she explained, came from drinking untreated stream water. The elders listened in silence. A week later, the oldest of them was seen filling his own pot at the tap.

Today the village keeps a small fund for repairs, and each household pays fifty naira a month. A committee of three men and three women looks after the borehole. Adaeze, now in JSS 3, says she has time to read before school. 'The tap gave us water,' she says, 'but it also gave us back our mornings.'

Question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Girls in villages are always late for school
A new borehole improved life and health in a village
Elders in Ugwuoba refused to drink any water
A health worker built a clinic in Ugwuoba
questions.explanation: The whole passage shows how the borehole changed daily life, school attendance and health.

The Dry Season Football Cup had reached the final, and the whole of Kawo seemed to have squeezed into the school field. Danladi stood at the edge of the penalty area, his heart beating like a drum at a wedding. One goal down, two minutes left. The ball came to him off a defender's knee, and for a moment the noise of the crowd vanished. He saw only the gap between the goalkeeper and the left post.

'I heard the shouting from here,' she said. 'Whoever scored that goal must be a proud boy.' Danladi smiled for the first time since the final whistle. Losing hurt, but he had given everything he had.

Many people believe that mobile phones should be banned in junior secondary schools. They argue that pupils spend lessons sending messages, that phones lead to cheating during tests, and that some children are bullied online by classmates. These are serious concerns, and every school must deal with them.

However, a total ban may not be the wisest answer. Phones can be used to look up the meaning of new words, to watch short science videos, and to contact parents in an emergency. A better approach would be clear rules: phones switched off and kept in bags during lessons, used only when a teacher allows it, and never brought into the examination hall. Pupils who break the rules could have their phones kept in the school office until a parent collects them.

Schools exist to prepare young people for the world they will live in. Teaching them to use technology responsibly is part of that preparation.

Question: The writer's main purpose is to
options: advertise a new brand of mobile phone
tell a story about a pupil who was bullied
describe how mobile phones are made
persuade readers that clear rules are better than a total ban on phones
questions.explanation: The writer weighs both sides and argues for rules instead of a ban.

questions.stem: Choose the word or phrase opposite in meaning to the word in capital letters: The class was in a state of CHAOS.
questions.explanation: Chaos means complete disorder; the opposite is order.

questions.stem: Choose the word or phrase opposite in meaning to the word in capital letters: The rich man is known to be GENEROUS.
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: When Bayo heard the news, he decided to BURY THE HATCHET with his cousin.
questions.explanation: To bury the hatchet means to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: Passing the examination with a distinction was a PIECE OF CAKE for Halima.
questions.explanation: A piece of cake means something very easy to do.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: The news of the strike came OUT OF THE BLUE.
questions.explanation: Out of the blue means suddenly and unexpectedly.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: The prefect was asked to KEEP AN EYE ON the younger pupils.
questions.explanation: To keep an eye on someone means to watch or look after them.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: Emeka has been BURNING THE MIDNIGHT OIL since the examination timetable came out.
questions.explanation: Burning the midnight oil means working or studying late at night.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: The manager said that, after the robbery, the shop was IN HOT WATER with the bank.
questions.explanation: In hot water means in trouble.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the idiom: The candidate's speech FELL ON DEAF EARS.
options: was heard by the deaf only
questions.explanation: If words fall on deaf ears, nobody pays attention to them.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The farmer used a ______ to cut the tall grass.
questions.explanation: A cutlass is used for cutting grass and bushes.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The person who examines patients' teeth is a ______.
questions.explanation: A dentist cares for teeth.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The ______ of the wedding read out the order of events.
questions.explanation: The master of ceremonies (MC) directs the programme.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: Ten years make a ______.
questions.explanation: A decade is ten years; a century is 100 and a millennium 1,000.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The pupils listened ______ as the visiting scientist explained how solar panels work.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to describe how they listened.

questions.stem: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: Necessary has one c and double s.

questions.stem: Which of these words is spelt correctly?
questions.explanation: Accommodation has double c and double m.

questions.stem: Select the option that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: Embarrass has double r and double s.

questions.stem: A word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and spelling is called a
questions.explanation: For example, "sea" and "see" are homophones.

questions.stem: Which prefix can be added to "legal" to give its opposite?
questions.explanation: The opposite of legal is illegal.

questions.stem: Which of the following words is a compound noun?
questions.explanation: Classroom is made from two words, class and room.

questions.topic: Writing to Highlight Main and Supporting Ideas
questions.stem: In a good paragraph, the sentence that states the main idea is called the
questions.explanation: The topic sentence tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

questions.topic: Writing to Highlight Main and Supporting Ideas
questions.stem: Which sentence would best support the topic sentence "Regular exercise is good for young people"?
options: It strengthens the heart and helps the body stay at a healthy weight.
Football is played in many countries.
The school field was cut last week.
Some pupils prefer reading to games.
questions.explanation: A supporting sentence gives a reason or example for the main idea.

questions.stem: A narrative composition mainly
options: tells a story of events in a sequence
argues for one side of an issue
questions.explanation: Narration means telling a story.

questions.stem: Which of these topics is best suited to a descriptive composition?
options: How I spent my last holiday
questions.explanation: Describing a place calls for descriptive writing.

questions.stem: An essay titled "How to prepare jollof rice" is an example of
questions.explanation: Expository writing explains or gives information on how something is done.

questions.stem: In a debate or argumentative essay, the speaker should
options: list the names of all the people present
give reasons and examples to support one side of the topic
questions.explanation: Argumentative writing tries to persuade with reasons and evidence.

questions.stem: Which is the most appropriate opening for a debate speech?
options: Dear Sir, I write to complain ...
Once upon a time, in a land far away ...
The Chairman, panel of judges, co-debaters, ladies and gentlemen, ...
questions.explanation: A debate speech begins by acknowledging the audience and the officials.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct complimentary close for a formal letter beginning "Dear Sir"?
questions.explanation: "Dear Sir" is paired with "Yours faithfully".

questions.stem: Which of these features is found in a formal letter but NOT in an informal letter?
questions.explanation: Formal letters include the address of the person or office being written to.

questions.stem: Which is the most suitable heading for a letter to the Chairman of a Local Government?
options: REQUEST FOR THE REPAIR OF THE ROAD TO OUR SCHOOL
questions.explanation: A formal letter has a short heading that states its purpose.

questions.stem: An informal letter would most likely be written to
questions.explanation: Informal letters are written to friends and relatives.

questions.stem: Which of these is a suitable opening sentence in a letter to your friend?
options: How are you and your family? I hope you are all well.
I write to apply for the post of clerk.
With reference to your letter of 4th May, ...
questions.explanation: An informal letter opens with friendly greetings.

questions.stem: In summary writing, you are usually asked to
options: write the main points in a stated number of sentences
write a poem about the passage
copy the passage word for word
add new points of your own
questions.explanation: A summary picks out only the essential points, briefly.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be left out of a summary?
questions.explanation: Examples, illustrations and repetitions are not part of a summary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: A flock is a group of sheep or birds, so it names a collection.

questions.stem: Identify the abstract noun in the sentence: "The honesty of the driver surprised the passengers."
questions.explanation: Honesty is a quality that cannot be seen or touched.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The ______ of the two classes were merged for the excursion.
questions.explanation: The plural of register is registers.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: All the ______ in the laboratory were washed after the practical.
questions.explanation: In compound nouns like test tube, the main noun (tube) takes the plural.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Each of my ______ owns a bicycle.
questions.explanation: The main word "brother" takes the plural in brother-in-law.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The farmer has a lot of ______.
questions.explanation: Equipment is uncountable and has no plural form.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The children's ______ were full of new books.
questions.explanation: A simple plural is needed here, not a possessive.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teacher nor the pupils ______ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "pupils", which is plural.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The news from the hospital ______ very encouraging.
questions.explanation: News is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: One of the girls ______ won a scholarship.
questions.explanation: The subject is "one", which is singular.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Yesterday Uche ______ the bus to Enugu.
questions.explanation: The past tense of take is took.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The bell has already ______.
questions.explanation: The past participle of ring is rung.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Every boy and girl ______ to wear a cap at the sports.
questions.explanation: "Every" makes the subject singular.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Of the three sisters, Amina is the ______.
questions.explanation: For more than two, use the superlative "tallest".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: This road is ______ than the one we used last week.
questions.explanation: The comparative of bad is worse.

questions.stem: Choose the option with the adjectives in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Opinion comes before size, and size before colour.

questions.stem: Identify the adjective in the sentence: "The tired workers rested under the tree."
questions.explanation: Tired describes the noun "workers".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The principal asked Ada and ______ to see him.
questions.explanation: Me is the object form needed after the verb "asked".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The money was shared between you and ______.
questions.explanation: After a preposition such as "between", the object pronoun is used.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: This is the man ______ car was stolen.
questions.explanation: Whose shows possession.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The boys hurt ______ while playing.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun for "boys" is themselves.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Everyone must bring ______ own textbook.
questions.explanation: "Everyone" is singular, so his or her is the traditional formal choice.

questions.stem: Identify the adverb in the sentence: "The choir sang beautifully at the end-of-year party."
questions.explanation: Beautifully tells how the choir sang.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She hardly ______ to school late.
questions.explanation: "Hardly" is already negative, so it is followed by "ever", and the verb agrees with "she".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He was ill, ______ he went to school.
questions.explanation: "Yet" shows contrast between being ill and going to school.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: You will not pass ______ you study hard.
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Musa stayed at home ______ it was raining heavily.
questions.explanation: "Because" introduces the reason.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The match was postponed ______ the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: "Because of" is followed by a noun phrase.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The pupils were congratulated ______ their success.
questions.explanation: We congratulate someone on something.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The cat jumped ______ the wall into the compound.
questions.explanation: "Over" shows movement across the top of something.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: My birthday is ______ 14th March.
questions.explanation: We use "on" with specific dates.

questions.topic: Identifying adverbials and tenses in passages
questions.stem: In the sentence "Every morning, the children walk to school", the adverbial is
questions.explanation: "Every morning" tells when the action happens.

questions.topic: Adverbials of frequency, intensifiers and manner
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverb of frequency?
questions.explanation: Usually tells how often something happens.

questions.topic: Adverbials of frequency, intensifiers and manner
questions.stem: In "The soup is extremely hot", the word "extremely" is
questions.explanation: Extremely strengthens the adjective "hot".

questions.stem: In "Mother kept the money under the mattress", "under the mattress" is an adverbial of
questions.explanation: It tells where the money was kept.

questions.stem: In "He left early to catch the first bus", the phrase "to catch the first bus" is an adverbial of
questions.explanation: It explains why he left early.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time the guests arrived, we ______ the food.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Look! The baby ______.
questions.explanation: "Look!" shows something happening now, so the present continuous is needed.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Our school ______ its inter-house sports next Friday.
questions.explanation: "Next Friday" refers to the future.

questions.topic: Constructing sentences with adverbials and tenses
questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have lived in Kaduna since 2019.
I have lived in Kaduna for 2019.
I am living in Kaduna since 2019.
questions.explanation: "Since" with a starting point goes with the present perfect.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences is in the passive voice?
options: The prefects are cleaning the windows.
The prefects will clean the windows.
The windows were cleaned by the prefects.
questions.explanation: In the passive voice, the subject receives the action and the doer follows "by".

questions.topic: Making sentences with active and passive verbs
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The new library ______ by the governor last week.
questions.explanation: The library received the action in the past, so we use the past passive.

questions.topic: Changing active to passive and vice versa
questions.stem: Change to the passive voice: "The dog chased the goat."
options: The goat is being chased by the dog.
The dog was chased by the goat.
The goat was chased by the dog.
questions.explanation: The object (goat) becomes the subject, and the tense stays in the past.

questions.topic: Changing active to passive and vice versa
questions.stem: Change to the passive voice: "The teacher will mark the scripts."
options: The scripts will mark the teacher.
The teacher will be marked by the scripts.
The scripts will be marked by the teacher.
The scripts were marked by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The future passive is will be + past participle.

questions.topic: Changing active to passive and vice versa
questions.stem: Change to the active voice: "The match was won by our school."
options: Our school was winning the match.
questions.explanation: The doer, "our school", becomes the subject.

questions.topic: Changing active to passive and vice versa
questions.stem: Change to the passive voice: "They are building a new hospital."
options: A new hospital is being built.
A new hospital is built by being.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive is is/are being + past participle.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: Ada said, "I am tired."
options: Ada said that I am tired.
Ada said that she is tired yesterday.
Ada said that she was tired.
Ada says that she was tired.
questions.explanation: "I" becomes "she" and "am" changes to "was" after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said to us, "Close your books."
options: The teacher said us to close our books.
The teacher asked that close our books.
The teacher told us to close our books.
The teacher told us close your books.
questions.explanation: Commands become "told + object + to + verb".

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He asked me, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me that where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.
He asked me where did I live?
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order becomes a statement and the tense moves back.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: Musa said, "I will come tomorrow."
options: Musa said that he would come the next day.
Musa said that I would come tomorrow.
Musa said that he will come tomorrow.
Musa said that he would came the next day.
questions.explanation: "Will" becomes "would" and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: You ______ wear a seat belt when you are in a moving car; it is the law.
questions.explanation: "Must" expresses an obligation.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ______ I borrow your pen, please?
questions.explanation: "May" is used politely to ask for permission.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: When I was five, I ______ swim, but now I can.
questions.explanation: "Could" is the past form of "can", for past ability.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: You look tired; you ______ go to bed early tonight.
questions.explanation: "Should" gives advice.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses a possibility?
options: You must submit your work today.
questions.explanation: "Might" shows that something is possible but not certain.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The lights are on, so somebody ______ be at home.
questions.explanation: "Must" here shows a strong logical conclusion.

questions.stem: In the sentence "She runs fast", the word "fast" is used as
questions.explanation: "Fast" tells how she runs, so it is an adverb here.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The fast car overtook us", the word "fast" is used as
questions.explanation: "Fast" describes the noun "car".

questions.stem: In the sentence "We waited until the rain stopped", the word "until" is a
questions.explanation: "Until" joins the two clauses.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Halima ______ her homework every evening before supper.
questions.explanation: A habitual action is expressed in the simple present: Halima does.

questions.stem: In the passive sentence "The letters were posted by Ike", who performed the action?
questions.explanation: The doer of the action follows "by" in a passive sentence.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: s(EA)t
questions.explanation: "Seat" and "key" both have the long vowel /i:/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: c(U)p
questions.explanation: "Cup" and "blood" both have /ʌ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: f(OO)d
questions.explanation: "Food" and "rule" have the long vowel /u:/; "foot" and "book" have the short /ʊ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: b(IR)d
questions.explanation: "Bird" and "word" both have /ɜ:/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: b(E)d
questions.explanation: "Bed" and "said" both have /e/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: h(O)t
questions.explanation: "Hot" and "what" both have /ɒ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: c(AR)
questions.explanation: "Car" and "heart" both have /ɑ:/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: l(AW)
questions.explanation: "Law" and "caught" both have /ɔ:/.

questions.stem: Which of these words contains a long vowel?
questions.explanation: "Sheep" has the long vowel /i:/; the others have the short /ɪ/.

questions.stem: Which word contains a short vowel?
questions.explanation: "Pull" has the short /ʊ/; the others have the long /u:/.

questions.stem: Which pair of words is different only in vowel length?
questions.explanation: "Fill" has short /ɪ/ and "feel" has long /i:/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: b(OY)
questions.explanation: "Boy" and "voice" both have the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: c(OW)
questions.explanation: "Cow" and "plough" both have /aʊ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: s(AY)
questions.explanation: "Say" and "weight" both have /eɪ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: g(O)
questions.explanation: "Go" and "road" both have /əʊ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: h(ERE)
questions.explanation: "Here" and "near" both have /ɪə/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in capital letters: ch(AIR)
questions.explanation: "Chair" and "pear" both have /eə/.

questions.stem: Which word contains the diphthong /aɪ/?
questions.explanation: "Kite" has /aɪ/, the sound in "my".

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in capital letters: (TH)in
questions.explanation: "Thin" and "thought" begin with the voiceless /θ/; "then" and "that" begin with voiced /ð/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in capital letters: (CH)emistry
questions.explanation: In "chemistry" and "character", ch is pronounced /k/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in capital letters: mea(S)ure
questions.explanation: "Measure" and "vision" both contain /ʒ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in capital letters: (SH)oe
questions.explanation: The s in "sugar" is pronounced /ʃ/, like sh in "shoe".

questions.stem: In which word is the letter "k" silent?
questions.explanation: In "knee" the k is not pronounced.

questions.stem: In which word is the letter "b" silent?
questions.explanation: The final b in "thumb" is silent.

questions.stem: Which word ends with the sound /t/?
questions.explanation: The -ed in "laughed" is pronounced /t/; in "played" it is /d/ and in "wanted" and "needed" it is /ɪd/.

questions.stem: In which word is the final "s" pronounced /ɪz/?
questions.explanation: After the sound /ks/ in "box", the plural ending is /ɪz/.

questions.stem: Which word begins with a consonant cluster?
questions.explanation: "Street" begins with three consonant sounds together: /str/. "Sh" and "ch" are single sounds.

questions.stem: Which word ends with a consonant cluster?
questions.explanation: "Desk" ends with /sk/, two consonant sounds together.

questions.stem: How many consonant sounds are there at the beginning of the word "splash"?
questions.explanation: "Splash" begins with /s/, /p/ and /l/.

questions.topic: Production of Vowel and Consonant Sounds
questions.stem: Sounds such as /p/ and /b/ are produced by closing and then opening the
options: back of the tongue and the soft palate
questions.explanation: /p/ and /b/ are bilabial sounds made with both lips.

questions.topic: Production of Vowel and Consonant Sounds
questions.stem: A vowel sound is produced when
options: the tongue touches the teeth firmly
the lips are pressed tightly together
air passes out only through the nose
air flows out of the mouth without being blocked
questions.explanation: Vowels are made with an open, unobstructed passage of air.

questions.stem: A phoneme is
options: the longest syllable in a word
the smallest unit of sound that can change the meaning of a word
a group of words with one meaning
questions.explanation: For example, /p/ and /b/ are different phonemes because "pin" and "bin" mean different things.

questions.stem: How many phonemes are there in the word "ship"?
questions.explanation: "Ship" is /ʃ/ + /ɪ/ + /p/: three sounds, although it has four letters.

questions.stem: Which word rhymes with "height"?
questions.explanation: "Height" and "kite" both end in /aɪt/.

questions.stem: Which of these words is stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: "Water" is said WAter; the other words are stressed on the second syllable.

questions.stem: Which of these words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: It is said imPORtant; the others are stressed on the first syllable: BEAUtiful, YESterday, TElephone.

questions.stem: In which word does the main stress fall on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: It is said phoTOgrapher, while PHOtograph, FAmily and MARketing are stressed on the first syllable.

questions.stem: Which of these words is stressed on the LAST syllable?
questions.explanation: It is said underSTAND; the others are stressed on the first syllable.

questions.stem: In which sentence is "record" stressed on the SECOND syllable?
options: Keep a record of your spending.
The pupils will record the song.
questions.explanation: As a verb, "reCORD" is stressed on the second syllable; as a noun it is "REcord".

questions.stem: A statement such as "I am going to the market" normally ends with a
questions.explanation: Ordinary statements end with a falling intonation.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences is normally said with a rising tune at the end?
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions usually end with a rising tune; wh-questions usually fall.

questions.stem: In the sentence "MUSA bought the new car", the emphatic stress on MUSA answers the question
options: Did Musa sell the new car?
Was the car Musa bought old?
questions.explanation: The stressed word gives the key information, here the person who bought it.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Ada ate the RICE", which question is being answered by the emphatic stress?
options: When did Ada eat the rice?
questions.explanation: Stress on RICE tells us what she ate.

questions.stem: The three main genres (types) of literature are
questions.explanation: Literature is usually grouped into prose, poetry and drama.

questions.stem: Literature can best be described as
options: imaginative writing or speech that expresses human experience in an artistic way
any list of names and telephone numbers
a set of rules for spelling
a record of a school's accounts
questions.explanation: Literature uses language creatively to show life and experience.

questions.stem: Oral literature is literature that
options: is passed from one generation to another by word of mouth
must be written by a famous author
is found only on the internet
questions.explanation: Oral literature is spoken, sung or chanted and handed down orally.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of oral literature?
questions.explanation: Riddles, proverbs, folktales and praise songs are forms of oral literature.

questions.stem: A long work of prose fiction with many characters and events is called a
questions.explanation: A novel is an extended work of prose fiction.

questions.topic: How literature reflects aspects of culture
questions.stem: A story in which a family performs a naming ceremony for a newborn baby on the eighth day mainly shows that literature
options: is always about kings and queens
reflects the customs and beliefs of a people
has no link with real life
is only meant to make people laugh
questions.explanation: Literature mirrors the culture of the society it comes from.

questions.stem: In many Nigerian folktales, the animal best known for cunning and trickery is the
questions.explanation: The tortoise is the famous trickster of many Nigerian folktales.

questions.stem: Anansi, the clever spider of many folktales, comes from the folklore of
questions.explanation: Anansi stories come from the Akan people of Ghana.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common feature of folktales?
options: animals that talk and behave like human beings
a list of chapters and footnotes
questions.explanation: Folktales often have animal characters with human qualities.

questions.stem: Many folktales begin with a set opening such as
questions.explanation: Traditional openings like "Once upon a time" are typical of folktales.

questions.stem: A folktale is described as didactic when it
options: is told in a foreign language
questions.explanation: Didactic means intended to teach.

questions.stem: In a folktale, the greedy tortoise eats all the food at a feast in the sky and falls to the ground, cracking his shell. The lesson of the story is that
options: feasts should be held in the sky
questions.explanation: The tortoise is punished for his greed.

questions.stem: Songs and choruses in folktales mainly serve to
options: entertain the audience and involve them in the telling
questions.explanation: Listeners join in the songs, which makes the telling lively.

questions.stem: In a folktale, a poor orphan finds a pot that fills itself with food every morning. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Self-filling pots are magical features common in folktales.

questions.stem: Folktales are mainly told
options: by elders to children, often in the evening
questions.explanation: Folktales are traditionally told by elders at gatherings, often at night by the fire.

questions.topic: Features of Nigerian and African folktales
questions.stem: In many Nigerian folktale sessions, the narrator says a line and the audience replies with a fixed response. This feature is called
questions.explanation: Call and response keeps the audience involved in the story.

questions.stem: Why do many African folktales end with a short statement such as "That is why the tortoise has a cracked shell"?
options: To give the date of the story
To explain the origin of something in nature
questions.explanation: Many tales explain how or why something came to be.

questions.stem: "The Tortoise and the Hare", in which the slow but steady runner wins the race, is one of the fables credited to
questions.explanation: The fable is traditionally credited to Aesop of ancient Greece.

questions.stem: In the European tale of Cinderella, which character uses magic to help her go to the ball?

The tone is warm and lively, and paragraphs are well linked.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Plastic waste has become one of the biggest problems facing our towns. Every day, sachets, bottles and bags are thrown into gutters and on to roadsides. When it rains, this waste blocks the drains, and water floods homes and shops. Plastics do not rot quickly; a single bottle may remain in the soil for hundreds of years. Animals such as goats sometimes eat plastic bags and die. Burning plastics is not a solution, because the smoke contains harmful chemicals that damage the lungs.

There are, however, ways to reduce the problem. Families can separate plastics from other refuse and sell them to recycling companies, which turn them into new products. Shoppers can carry reusable bags to the market. Schools can organise clean-up days and teach pupils the dangers of littering. Government can also enforce laws against dumping refuse in drains.

(a) In three sentences, one for each point, summarise the harmful effects of plastic waste mentioned in the passage. [9 marks]
(b) In two sentences, one for each point, state two ways of reducing the problem of plastic waste mentioned in the passage. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Plastic waste blocks drains and causes flooding
3 marks: (a) Plastic waste does not rot and stays in the soil for a very long time / animals that eat plastic bags die
3 marks: (a) Burning plastics releases harmful smoke that damages the lungs (any third distinct effect accepted)
3 marks: (b) Plastics can be separated and sold for recycling / people can use reusable bags
3 marks: (b) Schools can organise clean-up days and teach pupils / government can enforce laws against dumping (any second distinct way accepted)
questions.explanation: (a) Plastic waste blocks drains and causes floods. It does not rot, so it stays in the soil for hundreds of years. Animals that eat plastic bags die, and burning plastics produces smoke that harms the lungs. (b) Families can separate plastics and sell them for recycling, and shoppers can use reusable bags. Schools can hold clean-up days and the government can enforce laws against dumping refuse in drains.
